summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute confusion and weakness, found to be due to aspiration pneumonia in the setting of sepsis. He was febrile, tachycardic, and hypoxic on arrival, with imaging confirming left lower lobe consolidation. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, improved clinically, and was transitioned to oral levofloxacin for completion at home. During admission, he received IVIG and his fourth cycle of daratumumab for relapsed multiple myeloma. An elevated B-glucan level prompted infectious disease consultation, which favored a non-fungal cause. Two masses were noted: a slightly enlarged pelvic mass likely representing extramedullary hematopoiesis and a stable left inguinal mass possibly a hematoma, both requiring outpatient follow-up. His atrial tachycardia was managed with resumed diltiazem and carvedilol, and a single episode of urinary incontinence was attributed to medication sedation. He regained mental clarity, ambulated independently, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged.
problems: Multiple myeloma not having achieved remission
